approachQuestion.prompt:
Message Order

A mutable character array message contains lowercase English words separated by exactly one space, with no leading or trailing spaces. Rearrange the same array so that word order is reversed while letters within each word retain their order. Do not resize it. The empty array is also legal.

Constraints: 0 <= n = message.length <= 200000; indexed reads and swaps of characters take constant time.

Example 1: message represents "red gold blue" -> "blue gold red".
Example 2: "a bc" -> "bc a".
Example 3: "lamp" -> "lamp".
constraints: Choose the most efficient valid approach for the entire stated input domain; accept equivalent optimal variants.

options.text: Reverse the entire array using endpoint swaps. Scan for spaces and reverse each maximal word range using endpoint swaps.
options.feedback: The first reversal reverses word order and every word internally; reversing each word restores its letters.

options.text: Reverse the letters of every word in place, then reverse the entire array.
options.feedback: The whole-array reversal restores the letters and reverses the already arranged blocks, giving the same result.

options.text: Copy every word into a new list of strings, then write those words back in reverse list order, inserting single spaces.
options.feedback: The result is correct, but the word copies and list can be replaced by swaps within the supplied array.

options.text: Reverse the entire character array and return it without further changes.
options.feedback: For "ab c", it produces "c ba" instead of "c ab".

feedback.reason: Compose two reversals to change block order without changing each block internally.
details: Reverse all character positions in place. Scan to find each maximal range between spaces, including the final word, and reverse that range in place. An empty input needs no work.
Whole-array reversal fixes word order but reverses each word's letters. Reversing each maximal word range restores its internal order. The last word needs processing even without a trailing space.

“Reverse the entire array using endpoint swaps. Scan for spaces and reverse each maximal word range using endpoint swaps.”: The first reversal reverses word order and every word internally; reversing each word restores its letters.
“Reverse the letters of every word in place, then reverse the entire array.”: The whole-array reversal restores the letters and reverses the already arranged blocks, giving the same result.

“Copy every word into a new list of strings, then write those words back in reverse list order, inserting single spaces.”: The result is correct, but the word copies and list can be replaced by swaps within the supplied array.
“Reverse the entire character array and return it without further changes.”: For "ab c", it produces "c ba" instead of "c ab".

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method revealed after question 1, choose its tight worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Use a word-RAM model with constant-time indexed access and signed 64-bit arithmetic. Include all temporary buffers, input copies, and call frames; exclude supplied input and returned output. n is the character count. All reversals and scans are iterative with index ranges, no substrings or recursion. No hashing or amortized containers are used.
constraints: Analyze this fixed method regardless of your answer to question 1; choose the tightest pair.

options.text: O(n log n) time, O(1) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Global reversal and disjoint word reversals have linear total length.
details: The whole-array reversal visits n positions and the word reversals visit a total of at most n positions; finding word boundaries also scans n positions. Only a fixed number of indices and a swap temporary are used.

Use a word-RAM model with constant-time indexed access and signed 64-bit arithmetic. Include all temporary buffers, input copies, and call frames; exclude supplied input and returned output. n is the character count. All reversals and scans are iterative with index ranges, no substrings or recursion. No hashing or amortized containers are used.
“O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: This adds an input-sized buffer absent from the fixed method.
“O(n²) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: This counts repeated full scans that the fixed method does not perform.
“O(n log n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The fixed method does not perform sorting or independent binary searches.
